Written during the reign of Serfoji. See Raghavan, Venkataraman. Śāhendravilāsa of Śrīdhara Veṅkaṭeśa (A Poem on the Life of King Śāhaji of Tanjore, 1684-1710). Tiruchi: The Kalyan Press, 1952: p. 29.
Has a commentary by the author Vedakavīśvara (Vidyapariṇayavyākhyā)

'An allegorical drama like the Prabodhacandrodaya, in 7 acts. The plot is based on the marriage between the Jīvātman or the individual soul and Vidyā or spiritual wisdom. The drama is said to have been enacted on the occasion of the festival of goddess Ānandavallī, worshipped in Tanjore. See S. N. Dasgupta, HSL. Classical Period, Vol. I. pp. 486. 764.' New Catalogus Catalogurum (NCC). Vols 1-36: vol. 31, p. 147.
See New Catalogus Catalogurum (NCC). Vols 1-36: vol. 29, p. 132 for the alternative name Vidyāpariṇāma.
Descriptive Catalogue of Sanskrit Manuscripts in the Adyar Library (Adyar). Vols. 1–13: vol. 5, p. 491, mss. 1555–1556 are commentaries by Ānandarāyamakhin titled Vidyapariṇayavyākhyā.
